\[
\min_{\mathbf{y}}\; \frac{\lambda}{2} \sum_{i,j} \hat{W}_{ij} (y_i - y_j)^2 + \sum_i c_i (y_i - t_i)^2,\qquad
\Big(\lambda\,(D_m - D_n \bar{B} D_n) + \operatorname{diag}(S\mathbf{c})\Big)\, \mathbf{y} = S(\mathbf{c} \circ \mathbf{t}),\qquad
\hat{\mathbf{x}} = S^{\top} \mathbf{y}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\mathbf{t}\): The input channel
- \(\mathbf{c}\): The confidence of each pixel, 1 here
- \(\lambda\): The smoothness weight
- \(S\): The matrix that adds pixels into grid vertices
- \(\bar{B}\): The blur over neighboring vertices, [1, 2, 1] in each of the 5 dimensions
- \(D_n, D_m\): The diagonal scalings from bistochastization
- \(\mathbf{y}\): The values at the vertices

t is the input channel and c the confidence of each pixel, here 1 everywhere. The first sum asks for similar values where the bilateral affinity W is high: near in position and color. On the grid, S adds pixels into vertices and the blur B joins neighboring vertices. D_n and D_m come from bistochastization, which scales B so that its rows keep the pixel counts. The problem then becomes the sparse linear system shown, one unknown per vertex. Its solution y is sliced back to the pixels by S transposed.
